Think I might have found 2 small mistakes:

He popped it open and then rested both hands on the table, interlocking her fingers.

Shouldn't that be "his fingers"?

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Idk, I've always imagined Wondertainment not as lacking morals so much as having blue/orange morality. There do seem to be standards and priorities guiding Wondertainment's actions, but they're very alien and we have only vague ideas of what they might be.

That said, this is pretty dark. I like the idea that Wondertainment may be both desperate and under an unknown level of influence from the far more malevolent seeming Factory. For unknown reasons he needs an heir *right now* no matter the cost, someone who can do something he can't, which is pretty terrifying given how powerful he already was.

I had never put much thought into how Wondertainments came to be (like dwarves, they always sorta just popped up out of the ground in my head), so when I read this last night I was taken aback a bit.

Not so much now on a re-read. I like this a whole lot more than the first time, and I liked it a lot then.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
My, uh… my intended point was that it's way, way worse than just dying. And yes, he does this fully intentionally. Because A) He's dying and very desperate and/or B) The Factory is affecting him in a very negative way.

Even ignoring the context of The Factory messing with his brainparts, Wondertainment has never been characterized as a particularly… moral entity.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: My own definition of death is "erasure of one's mind from this realm of existence." Felicia's body might be fine, but her mind has been destroyed and/or sent to the afterlife, as have the minds of the other Little Misters. I know it's semantics, but it's still murder to me.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Dr. Wondertainment is fucked up. Like, the old one, not Isabel; she's innocent. He just straight murdered a young woman in order to create his replacement. Hell, he murdered dozens of people to make the Little Misters. I don't know if the horror was intentional, so I don't think I can upvote until I know the purpose of the tale.

That being said, the writing IS good, so I don't think my (temporary) novote will hurt this Tale's success.
